{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjqe88AAAABZln3Rg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3INzhDMKnA", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IN", "number": 125, "title": "Add evidence-qualified browser-local native file mail with exact-byte acquisition", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `34f1d70929af5fc30af8330c879808c39efff2a4`, users can send immediate, multi-recipient and scheduled text letters, but cannot send a file to a local resident or retrieve its original bytes. This omits a documented PC-VAN mail capability.

`src/storage/schema.ts` requires text subject/body fields and rejects additional mail fields. `createHumanMail` in `src/storage/repository.ts` accepts text only. `src/storage/controls.ts::downloadFile` UTF-8-encodes strings, which cannot preserve arbitrary binary files. Existing OSL acquisition demonstrates confirmed downloads but remains a separate service.

This extends previously deferred functionality; it is not a regression in the completed scheduled-text-mail scope.

## Expected outcome

Provide one complete immediate native file-mail journey through the existing MAIN `1`, MAIN `X` and DAISIZEN `MAIL` contexts:

Select an existing local resident → explicitly open a browser file picker → select one bounded file → review recipient identity, subject, safe filename and exact byte count → confirm → inspect the saved letter in SENT/READ → reload or export/restore → explicitly acquire identical bytes.

Represent a distinct file-bearing letter. Do not imply authenticated MIME attachment semantics or require mixed text/file composition. Keep routine Japanese terminal output concise and place historical qualifications in About and documentation.

For this increment, accept files from zero through 262,144 bytes. Use a documented, bounded safe basename/export-name rule. These are application limits, not historical PC-VAN limits. Preserve payload bytes without decoding, transcoding, decompression, execution or inline rendering.

Scope is one selected human sending one new file letter to one existing local resident. Incoming resident files, file replies, scheduled files, multiple recipients, Internet transport/uuencoding, OSL expansion, retention changes and XMODEM/Quick-VAN emulation remain outside scope.

## Context

Historical evidence inspected on 2026-10-24:

- [NEC PC-VAN office account, March 1993, printed p. 231](https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/jkg/43/3/43_KJ00002959297/_pdf/-char/ja): explicitly describes spreadsheet/word-processor binary files and XMODEM/Quick-VAN support. High confidence for the documented earlier capability; continuity into late 1996 is a moderate-confidence inference. It supplies no target-year selection, listing or cancellation sequence. OCR spacing is damaged.
- [PC_VAN.SCR catalog excerpt](https://search.vector.co.jp/vsearch/vsearch.php?kanji=euc&key=SCR&start=260): indexed author description lists text/binary mail retrieval and mail uploading, alongside a March 2, 1996 date. [Package metadata](https://www.vector.co.jp/soft/dl/win31/net/se007553.html) attributes version 1.25 to the same date. Both remain search-index evidence; direct description/metadata retrieval failed. This is qualified target-year corroboration, not proof of host commands or each feature's introduction date.
- [Participant account, “大量データの入力,” supplementary material 3](https://www.dl.slis.tsukuba.ac.jp/DLjournal/No_16/10-furushou/10-furushou.html): now directly readable. Instructions associated with a December 1995 work item explicitly distinguish former PC-VAN binary-mail submission from replacement FTP submission. Moderate confidence as firsthand workflow evidence. The work-item date does not establish the instructions' publication date; project filename/compression rules are not host-wide requirements.
- [Internet Magazine, November 1996, p. 221](https://iwparchives.jp/wp-content/themes/twentytwelve/bn/pdf/im199611-220-mail2.pdf): documents PC-VAN outbound Internet-file uuencoding. This concerns a separate gateway facility. Its Internet-mail size table must not become a native-file-mail limit, and its sending-only conversion qualification does not establish a general inability to receive mail.

Accepted reconstruction: browser-local storage and picker/download integration, one-file representation, commands, prompts, limits, safe filenames, layout and acquisition from the sender's saved copy. No exact historical controls are claimed. Exact late-1996 mailbox relationships and transfer procedures remain unresolved without blocking this disclosed subset.

Implementation precedents are `src/commands.ts` input ownership and revision fences, transactional numbering/retry handling in `src/storage/repository.ts`, and confirmed OSL acquisition. Inspect `src/ai/mail.ts::pairMail`, planning, target validation and repository commit checks: merely adding a file field would otherwise admit file letters into existing text-mail context and reply planning.

Duplicate check: repository-scoped open-Issue/open-PR queries returned no items. All-state binary searches recovered earlier exclusions, including [Issue #89](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/89), [#93](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/93) and [#97](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/97); the Japanese バイナリ query returned none. [Issue #123](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/123) explicitly excludes attachments. Searches are terminology-dependent and inventory may change.

Existing validation evidence: [PR #124](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/pull/124) and `docs/validation.md` report a final cold-cache complete run of 501 passing checks with three workers, including configured type checking/build, and disclose preceding failures/corrections. The implementation-head and merge trees match locally. These are Coordinator records; this research graph did not execute checks. Default-worker reliability and the earlier missing-prompt failure's exact cause remain unresolved.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- Implement the complete journey above in all three existing mail entry contexts, preserving their contextual returns and selected-human identity. Resolve and pin the resident ID before review; renames or list reordering must not redirect the letter. Anonymous entry may reuse existing optional registration.
- File selection requires an explicit user action. Picker cancellation, empty selection, read errors, oversized files and rejected filenames create no mail or payload records. Explain the actionable error and permit reselection or cancellation. Validate actual bytes and count again at the persistence boundary.
- Review shows the pinned recipient, subject, export filename and exact byte count. Approval saves once. Editing/reselection requires renewed review. Duplicate approval, queued input and uncertain save acknowledgement must not duplicate letters; changed payload or metadata under an existing retry identity must be rejected.
- Persist payload and metadata atomically with mail numbering using existing repository conventions. Quota/transaction failures leave no partial file, letter or consumed number and permit an intentional retry. Concurrent text, scheduled-release and file-mail writes retain unique numbering.
- Use a validated JSON-round-trippable byte representation compatible with existing backups. Legacy backups without file mail remain valid. Reject malformed encoding, mismatched size, excessive payloads, unsafe names, invalid member references and unsupported file-mail combinations before changing the current world. Cover direct repository writes as well as import. Reset/restore must include or remove the corresponding bytes atomically.
- SENT/LIST and READ clearly identify file mail and show metadata without dumping payload into terminal output, logs or command history. Acquisition requires a separate confirmation pinned to the saved letter and payload; list/read/help/reload never trigger a download. Acquire as inert binary data with the documented safe filename. Cancelled, repeated, failed and stale acquisition approvals produce no unintended download and preserve contextual navigation.
- Invalidate pending selection, file reads, review, saves and acquisition across reset/import, selected-human changes and existing controller invalidation boundaries, including asynchronous waits and cross-tab replacement. Preserve terminal focus, queued-input and simulated IME protections.
- Keep file letters, including subject, filename, size and payload, outside all resident-generation prompt excerpts and automatic mail-target planning for this increment. Reject attempts to use file letters as resident reply/read-confirmation parents, including restored or already-planned work. Sending, inspecting and acquiring a file must not create recipient-read evidence or guarantee a reply. Preserve existing text-mail pair privacy, budgets, schedules and confirmation semantics.
- Extend existing Playwright/real-IndexedDB coverage. Compare downloaded bytes with original fixtures containing NUL, all byte values, invalid UTF-8 and mixed line endings; include zero-byte and boundary-size cases. Verify exact bytes after reload and JSON export/restore, cancellation/error paths, rollback, retry collisions, concurrent numbering, invalid/legacy restoration, stale approvals and prompt isolation. Use synthetic files and mocked inference only.
- Exercise the production keyboard journey through all three mail routes, including acquisition and restoration. Preserve affected functional, storage, consent, IME and terminal regression coverage. Reuse `tests/mail*.spec.ts`, `tests/scheduled-mail.spec.ts`, `tests/storage-controls.spec.ts`, composition/terminal coverage and OSL download patterns as appropriate; no new framework is needed.
- The Coordinator must run focused checks and the existing complete suite before merge, normally `npm test -- --workers=3`; its configuration performs TypeScript checking and production bundling. Follow README setup as needed. Report actual workers, failures, corrections, skipped/unperformed checks and limitations. Review the final diff and check whitespace/documentation links. Do not require real inference or a model download.
- Update mail/storage documentation, discoverable help/About and the historical research record with supported observations, dates, confidence, inaccessible sources, accepted reconstructions and deferred receiving/protocol behavior. Preserve existing OSL/FTP text downloads and all current text-mail journeys.

## Optional validation

Native IME observation and another browser engine may provide additional confidence. Historical-user feedback or a recovered dated manual may refine controls later. Neither is a completion gate for this bounded reconstruction.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
